How it unfolded 20 July 2025 A Mississippi federal judge blocks the state's anti-DEI law with a temporary restraining order. 22 July 2025 The State flags errors. The order is replaced with a corrected version, dated 20 July; the mistakes are called "clerical". 18 August 2025 A preliminary injunction adopts that reasoning, still citing a case that doesn't exist. October 2025 Asked by a US Senator, the judge says a law clerk used an AI tool (Perplexity) on a draft. 22 October 2026 The Fifth Circuit vacates the injunction and orders the case reassigned to another judge. Not the first AI-tainted order 1 New Jersey, 2025. A federal judge withdrew an opinion with fabricated quotations; he later said a law-school intern had used ChatGPT. 2 Georgia, 2025. An appeals court vacated a divorce order that relied on fake cases, traced to a lawyer's draft the trial court had adopted. ! The accountability gap. Commentators reviewing these cases found no judge disciplined so far. Lawyers get sanctioned; judges' orders just get set aside. The common thread: AI output passed from a clerk, intern or lawyer's draft into a signed order without anyone checking the sources. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 04 / 08

What our courts have said KERALA HIGH COURT POLICY · JULY 2025 · DISTRICT JUDICIARY AI can assist, not decide No AI for findings, reliefs, orders or judgments. No case data in cloud chatbots. Verify every output, citations included, and keep an audit record of AI use. SUPREME COURT DRAFT REGULATIONS ON AI IN COURTS, 2026 Human primacy, officer accountability Reg. 20: no outcome by algorithm alone; no AI risk scores for bail. Reg. 8(1): accountability rests "exclusively" on the officer; hallucinations are no excuse. Reg. 43(3): parties declare AI use in submissions. The SC regulations were released in draft on 3 June 2026 (comments closed 15 July). They take effect only once the SC and each High Court notify them. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 05 / 08

Five fixes before the draft is final 1 Non-waivable checks for judgments. The draft (Reg. 8(3)) lets an officer skip verification for recorded reasons. Every citation and quotation in an order should be checked, without exception. 2 Cover drafting. Disclosure to parties covers case management and administration; it should also cover AI help in drafting orders. 3 A chambers protocol. Researcher drafts, a second person checks sources against the record, the judge signs. 4 Open corrections. Errors fixed by a recorded order, never a silent replacement or a backdated copy. 5 Notify it. Clear rules, adopted by every High Court, protect judges as much as litigants. Adv. TA K E AWAY AI can draft. Only a judge can decide. When fabricated material reaches a signed order, the cost is more than one case: it is public confidence in the courts. India has a good draft framework. It now needs firm verification rules, notified and followed. Adv.
